scope: Two system-level fixes on Page 24 (Vidra fresh design system, 883:84247) left open by critique-fixes-remaining-2026-10-15.json: the Vidra Fresh / Slider unfilled track, and the opacity-only State=Disabled variants of Icon button, Toggle, Checkbox, Field, Slider, Password field and Menu item. approach: Read-only census first: every non-archive instance of the Slider and of the seven Disabled variants on Pages 24-29, with its surface, visibility and override fields and values.

Every write switched to and asserted its page, rejected nodes outside that page or inside an Archive section, collected and validated all targets (type, name, main component, current bound variable, opacity) before the first mutation, and returned the previous values recorded below.
Only Vidra Fresh / Interface variables were bound. Paints were rebound with the variable's resolved colour, so no stale cached colours were introduced.
One temporary probe (two throwaway instances 1684:90256 and 1684:90261, created and removed in the same script on Page 24) confirmed that new instances inherit the source icon colour.
Application code is out of scope. This record is the only repository file added; no existing record was edited.

sliderTrack.token: color/hover (#333333) replaces color/control (#262626) for the unfilled Track in all 27 variants
sliderTrack.why: color/hover is the only Fresh surface step above canvas, panel and raised that is not an outline or content colour; it is the value the earlier pass used for the Mask controls and B06 patches, so those overrides became redundant and were removed.
sliderTrack.limit: The unfilled track is visible on every surface a slider sits on, but stays below a 3:1 non-text ratio. Fresh has no token between color/border (#363636) and color/muted (#949494); reaching 3:1 on raised would need a new token near #6f6f6f, and color/muted would leave only 1.53:1 between the filled and unfilled parts.

disabledRecipe.rule: State=Disabled renders at full opacity. The control's own surface becomes color/panel with a 1px color/border inside outline. Everything that carries meaning (label, value, icon, check or minus glyph, toggle knob, slider value and thumb) becomes color/muted. A control or inline action with no resting surface keeps none.

perComponent.Icon button: panel surface, border outline, muted icon (same as the End frame action icon surface)
perComponent.Toggle Off and On: panel track, border outline, muted knob; the knob position still shows the value
perComponent.Checkbox Off, On, Mixed: panel box, existing border outline, muted check or minus; the glyph still shows the value
perComponent.Field: panel surface, border outline, muted value
perComponent.Password field: panel surface, border outline, muted dots; the inline Show action becomes muted text with no pill (it has no pill when enabled, and a bordered pill inside a bordered field doubled the outline and overflowed 40px fields)
perComponent.Menu item: no surface or outline (the row has none at rest; a bordered panel row in a raised menu would read as selected), muted icon and label
perComponent.Slider: track stays color/hover, value and thumb become color/muted

3_consumerOverrides.why: Icon colour overrides set inside the Icon button and Menu item variants do not reach existing instances whose swap-bound icon slot holds its own icon instance (fresh instances do inherit). Those consumers kept white or secondary icons, so their icon strokes were set to color/muted explicitly, at the highest component that owns them so nested copies inherit. Selected-state consumers already carry explicit black icon overrides for the same reason.

figmaBehaviour: Nested icon colour overrides in a variant do not propagate to existing instances whose INSTANCE_SWAP-bound icon was set on the instance; new instances, including ones switched from Default to Disabled, do inherit them.
removeOverrides() takes effect after the script's synchronous edits, so a rename in the same script is lost; the layer name had to be restored in a second call.

Overrides whose value equals the inherited value are pruned when an instance is next recomputed (icon width and height entries disappeared with geometry unchanged), but an override written in the same script as the source change is still listed.
